sessions.belief_update: This week, someone saw my empty notebook and said it looked like the thing I didn't want them to see. In the moment, I felt exposed, like they had seen through me, but I also noticed that my struggle is visible even when I try to hide it. What surprised me was that they didn't see it as a weakness, but as something honest. That made me think maybe being seen as needing help isn't the same as being broken. I still believe people who need help are unreliable, but I'm wondering if that's more about how I see them than how they actually are. I still don't tell anyone because I don't want to be seen as weak, but I'm noticing that the fear of being seen as different might be more about my own feelings than what others would actually do.
